title: Stormwatch rollcall and release summit notes — 2026-11 (draft)
content:
Purpose and context:
This is the working capture from the Stormwatch rollcall + release summit (compact preflight) for the micro-cohort deploy 2026-11. This doc combines the hour-by-hour watchlist, preflight checklist, smoke sampler, and an early draft of the release notes we’ll push to internal customers. Use as the single source during the 48h runway; treat items marked FAST as highest priority.

High-level goal:
- Ship feature bundle: model-routing affinity + safe-shed fallback + reduced cold-start for kv-cache.
- Maintain P99 latency delta <= +30ms vs baseline and error rate < 0.1% for production traffic during cohort.

Owners (primary contacts):
- Release steward: Aisha Patel (oncall pager: @aisha)
- Canary shepherd: Marco Delgado
- Telemetry & alerts: Sofia Chen
- SRE escalation liaison: Liam O'Rourke
- Customer comms: Priya Rao (GTM)

Quick watch timeline (48h, local PST):
- T-48h: Preflight dry run (ops lab) — smoke tests + telemetry sanity (Aisha, Marco)
- T-24h: Config freeze; roll steward sign-off; announce quiet window (all)
- T-6h: Nightwatch handoff readout; validation cohort schedule loaded (Marco -> Liam)
- T+0h: Canary start (0.5% traffic) and first 15m smoke sample
- T+1h: Canary status check; expand to 5% if green
- T+6h: Full cohort (25%) if sustained green signals
- T+24h: Post-rollout data capture window; stability decisions (keep / scale / rollback)

Preflight checklist (FAST flags first):
- [FAST] Build artifact verified in staging and matches commit: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime@v2026.11.0-rc3 (Marco)
- [FAST] Canary config applied and circuit-breakers set (SLOs) (Marco)
- [FAST] Telemetry dashboards baked: latency histogram, error-rate, inferred-quality-regressions (Sofia)
- [FAST] Pager rotations set; escalation ladder posted in #release-stormwatch (Aisha)
- Health checks and smoke routines: ensure endpoints for /healthz, /kv-warm, /model-prefetch respond under 250ms in staging (Liam)
- DB migration? none declared. If any schema changes appear, deferrable migration-only flag must be true and run in maintenance window (owner: data-eng)
- Secrets & certs: KMS key rotation check and vault access validated for private deployments (security)
- Canary rollback plan drafted and validated: immediate traffic cut + redirect to fallback model variant + cache flush budgeted (Marco)
- Customer-impact matrix populated (Priya)
- Release notes draft (see below) available to internal docs and legal review (Aisha)

Smoke sampler (quick tests to run at T+0, T+15m, T+1h):
- Generate 20 example prompts across short/long sequences; assert end-to-end latency and token rate counters
- Validate KV-prefetch hit-rate increment > 10% for warmed keys in sampling window
- Forced-fallback test: temporarily throttle primary model to trigger fallback routing; assert degrade path works without 5xxs
- Observability test: inject synthetic trace id and confirm it surfaces in tracing UI within 30s

Telemetry & gating rules (automatic and manual):
- Automatic rollback triggers:
  - 5xx surge > 0.5% sustained for 5m
  - P99 latency > baseline + 80ms over 10m
- Manual hold/rollback triggers (require steward + SRE ack):
  - Increased hallucination score on eval prompts (Sofia)
  - Regressions in cost-per-token > 15% vs forecasted binning

Early draft of release notes (internal-facing):
- Title: Model routing affinity + fallback and KV warm optimizations (2026-11)
- Overview: This release introduces routing affinity that favors warmed model variants for repeat sessions, a graceful fallback path when capacity is constrained, and several engine-level optimizations to reduce cold-start time for KV caches.
- Impact: Expected to reduce median token latency by 6–12% for repeat session workloads and reduce cold-start tail latency by up to 40% in high concurrency situations. Cost per token forecast: neutral to slight improvement depending on batch mix.
- Known limitations: Fallback routing will add additional model-variant cost when capacity dips; metrics might undercount short-lived KV fills during first 6 hours of cohort.
- Migration notes: No customer action required. Private deployments with strict HSM key rotation must re-validate vault bindings after upgrade.
- Rollback: Rolling rollback will re-enable previous routing table and force cache flush. Contact release steward for assistance.

Risks & mitigations (short list):
- Risk: Fallback flood causing unexpected token-cost spike. Mitigation: throttle fallback expansions and use billing meter alerts (Sofia).
- Risk: Telemetry mismatch between staging and prod due to sampled traces. Mitigation: increase sampling rate for 2h after cohort to validate signals (Liam).
- Risk: Customer-visible latency blips during expansion. Mitigation: stagger expansion windows and keep canary at steady-state for at least 1h before each increase (Marco).

Open questions / action items (TODO):
- [ ] Confirm export window for telemetry retention increase (+24h) with infra (Sofia) — due 2026-11-04
- [ ] Finalize customer comms blurb and internal FAQ (Priya) — due T-12h
- [ ] Decide whether to enable quantized-variant in dedicated pools (perf/ops decision) — assignees: perf-team, due pre-T-24h
- [ ] Add a short postmortem drill to the 72h stabilization cadence (Aisha) — tracking ticket RE-2160

Communication & channels:
- Slack: #release-stormwatch (primary), #sre-oncall (escalation)
- Pager rota: standard oncall; backup is cross-team (SRE-rotation)
- Broadcast template for incidents: 1) short summary 2) scope 3) action taken 4) ETA to resolution

Post-release notes (what we’ll capture after T+24h):
- Hourly P99 and error-rate snapshots for first 24h
- Telemetry slices by region and model-variant (to spot drift)
- Sampled prompt/response quality checks vs eval set
- Cost delta report vs forecasted baseline (finance tag: release-costs)

Appendix: quick commands & smoke snippets
- curl -sS -H "x-trace-id: stormwatch-test" https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/healthz
- k get pods -n canary | grep affinity && k logs -f canary-policy

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the first expansion slow; we lose nothing by waiting an extra 20m if the telemetry clarity improves.
- If trace sampling looks off, toggle sample-rate to 100% for 30m and then revert. Be prepared for extra ingestion cost.

Ear-marked tickets for reference:
- RE-2143 (canary config + gating), RE-2160 (postmortem drill), RE-2188 (telemetry retention bump)
